page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.48xlarge is a dedicated, storage-optimized instance designed for large-scale data systems. Powered by Intel Xeon 8559C processors on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs operating at a nominal clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The memory subsystem consists of 1,536 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB per physical core. Built-in storage features a dense array of 120,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. It contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark metrics position the instance within the highest tiers for data operations and multi-core computing. In synthetic evaluations, it records a PassMark CPU score of 131,650.09 and multi-core stress-ng throughput of 169,940.36, both falling in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Memory subsystem evaluations demonstrate 571.21 GB/sec of uncached read throughput and 240.52 GB/sec of write throughput across large blocks. Database and transaction-oriented benchmarks show 35,725.42 points in PassMark database operations and 203.2 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, accompanied by static web serving bandwidth measuring 214.44 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the instance stems from its fixed resource footprint: the absence of GPU acceleration precludes accelerated training workloads, and the monolithic 120 TB storage bundle demands sustained high utilization to remain cost efficient. From a qualitative perspective, the consolidation of massive NVMe storage, broad DDR5 memory capacity, and dedicated compute reduces the network overhead and costs typical of detached block storage architectures. It functions effectively for petabyte-scale distributed database nodes, high-throughput caching clusters, operational real-time analytics, and data warehousing extraction, transformation, and loading pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.48xlarge is a storage-optimized instance engineered for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by a 96-core Intel Xeon 8559C processor delivering 192 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture via the Nitro hypervisor, the platform integrates 1,536 GB of DDR5 memory and 120,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network interface capacity scales to a 200 Gbps baseline. Empirical benchmarks confirm elite multi-threaded throughput, recording top-tier results in PassMark database operations and multi-core CPU workloads. In-memory transaction capability is evidenced by 203.2 million Redis SET operations per second and 571.21 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. While lacking discrete GPU hardware, the platform delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency by consolidating extreme I/O capacity and large memory reserves onto a single node, removing network storage latency. The architecture aligns directly with large distributed databases, transactional datastores, massive analytics engines, and enterprise ETL pipelines.
